<objective>
Close CONTEXT.md D-04's repo half. Fold the six Copywriting Contract rows that Phase 01 recorded in
`01-UAT.md` into `01-UI-SPEC.md` § Copywriting Contract, then delete the standing exception those
missing rows forced into `lib/copy.ts` — the four per-key doc comments and the header paragraph that
qualifies the file's own premise.

Purpose: `lib/copy.ts` opens by claiming a reviewer can diff it against the contract instead of grepping
JSX, then immediately qualifies that claim because six keys had nowhere to point. Phase 01 could not fix
it — `01-UI-SPEC.md` is a checker-approved artifact plan 01-17 did not own. **01.1 owns it**, and D-04
says so explicitly. Leaving the exception in place after the rows land means the file documents a
divergence that no longer exists, which is the same class of error WR-06 was opened for.

Output: `01-UI-SPEC.md` with the owed rows, `lib/copy.ts` with an unqualified header, and a source-scan
tripwire that keeps deck and contract in step.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It supplies the copy the venue and auth
surface re-skins (plans 01.1-09 and 01.1-10) consume, which is why it sits in wave 1 rather than after them.

**D-04's other half is not here.** The lexicon re-cut is almost entirely an edit to the design project's
`readme.md` — a repo grep for the dropped vocabulary returned 16 matches, **all ordinary English in code
comments** ("this covers the unauthenticated case", "the idle timer fired"). Zero user-visible strings use
restaurant jargon. Task 2 verifies that finding rather than trusting it; the write-back is plan 01.1-14.
</objective>

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| copy deck → unauthenticated user | `COPY.errors.*` strings render to anonymous visitors on the signup, login and reset surfaces. Their wording is a security control, not decoration. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-05 | Information Disclosure | `COPY.errors.auth` shared signup/login error string | high | mitigate | The string is deliberately ambiguous to resist account enumeration (T-02-01 in `01.1-RESEARCH.md` § Security Domain, ASVS V7). Task 1 changes no string value — asserted by a `git diff` gate — and task 2 pins the literal with a failure message stating why. |
| T-01.1-17 | Repudiation | `01-UI-SPEC.md` edited without provenance | medium | mitigate | The added rows carry an inline note naming D-04 as the authorisation and Phase 01.1 as the owner, so the edit to a checker-approved artifact is auditable rather than anonymous. |
| T-01.1-18 | Tampering | Copy deck drifting from its contract unnoticed | medium | mitigate | `tests/lib/copy-contract.test.ts` asserts every deck string has a contract row, with a non-vacuity guard on the extracted table so a broken extractor cannot produce a silent green. |
</threat_model>
